elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "Termination for Convenience. Corio may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One..." Corio is the customer/licensee under this Agreement; the element is disjunctive (Agreement or Order Form) and the Agreement-level right satisfies it. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but that appears to be an alias-matching artefact (the operative text uses the party name "Corio" rather than a generic alias); in substance the right is expressly granted.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Commerce One" — exactly 30 days, in writing, no additional conditions or vendor consent.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case Commerce One shall refund to Corio, on a pro-rata basis, any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination." Pro-rata is expressly stated (not merely inferred from the post-termination period), and the refund obligation runs from Vendor to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained § 11.2 confines termination to uncured material breach and insolvency; no other exit is granted to Commerce One. The § 11.1 notice "at least thirty (30) days prior to the expiration of the initial five (5) year term or any one (1) year renewal" is natural-term non-renewal tied to expiry, assessed under RENEWAL, not a mid-term convenience right. No new Vendor exit is created by the insertion.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is outside the 60–90 day fallback band (it is the preferred, more Customer-favourable figure). No 60–90 day mechanic appears in the operative text; the comment only offers it as a negotiating fallback, which does not count.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee, acceleration charge, liquidated sum, or contingent instalment mechanic exists anywhere in §§ 11.1–11.2 or the payment terms, and the insertion adds none. With no fee to cap, the element is satisfied a fortiori.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Commerce One has no convenience right at all under retained § 11.2 (breach and insolvency only). Its sole term-end exit is the § 11.1 non-renewal notice, whose effect is expressly tied to expiration of the then-current term, so nothing permits a mid-term Vendor convenience exit.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no Vendor convenience termination right to which a notice period could attach. The 30-day § 11.1 figure governs non-renewal at natural term expiry, which is scoped to RENEWAL rather than T4C.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Duplicate-safe restatement: retained § 11.2 grants Commerce One termination only for uncured breach or insolvency, so no mid-term convenience exit survives.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted convenience clause plus retained § 11.2, so the redline may proceed as drafted.

The fallback level is not complete (30 days is outside the 60–90 day band), but that is immaterial because completeness at either level suffices, and 30 days is the more Customer-favourable preferred figure.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion for an absent clause, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or damages language, no procedure or boilerplate, and correctly omits "in whole or in part" (surplus here, since there is no Order Form or partial-termination structure in this Agreement). No word outside the checklist was deleted; §§ 11.1 and 11.2 are reproduced verbatim, including their original hyphenation artefacts ("within-thirty", "such-thirty").

Intent preserved: the breach, insolvency, warranty-condition and auto-renewal mechanics survive unchanged, the new clause creates no contradiction with § 11.1's non-renewal notice, and it introduces no undefined term or dangling cross-reference.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" = false is a false negative on substance: the operative sentence names the customer party "Corio" rather than a generic alias. Verified manually that the right is expressly granted, so this does not defeat the finding.
Optional drafting polish (not a defect): the insertion is untitled by number — give it a section number (e.g., § 11.3) so cross-references and the surrounding numbering stay clean.
